front: When does a correction change profit?
back: When one side of the correcting entry is an income or expense account and the other is not (asset, liability, capital, drawings or suspense).

front: Asset debited to an expense account
back: Correcting it increases profit and increases non-current assets.
Correcting it increases profit and increases current assets by the same amount.

front: Carriage outwards debited to carriage inwards
back: Correcting it increases gross profit; profit for the year is unchanged.
Draft profit + corrections that increase profit − corrections that reduce profit = corrected profit.

front: Error of commission between two customers
back: No effect on profit or on total trade receivables.
